liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playin' In The Band** (3 reviews): Reviewer singles out this version as a nice one; The band plays with high energy, flying through the sections where Donna usually draws cringes [8][13][17]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Reviewer picks this China Cat as one of the nice performances; Reviewer calls the China Cat into Rider great, with outstanding Jerry playing [8][14]
- **U.S. Blues** (2 reviews): A great U.S. Blues is followed by a nice jam, with Promised Land and Brokedown Palace mid-second set; Reviewer cites U.S. Blues into Promised Land as an example of the band exploring rarely visited territory [14][18]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleoo** (1 review): Reviewer points to the Half-Step into It Must Have Been The Roses as adventurous playing [18]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Reviewer wonders if this is the greatest version, calling it definitely top ten [18]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Reviewer finds this Brokedown Palace sounds wonderful [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-07-27.132188.southern.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 163 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1974-07-27.akgd200e.unk.sirmick.132282.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 167 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Brief wow and flutter remains at the start of U.S. Blues, in Playin' In The Band, and in I Know You Rider [2]
- **gd1974-07-27.sbd.miller.107804.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [3]
- **gd74-07-27.sbd.kaplan.2420.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 144 min; rated 3.85/5 by 27 [5]. Said about its sound: Wide stereo separation, strong vocals and plenty of fine detail in cymbals, keys and Bobby's guitar, despite a cassette flaw; Phil sounds bouncy; Jerry's guitar sits lower in the mix than some would like but still gets loud; Master seems slightly fast, suggesting a pitch problem [7][10][12][16][17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer insists Donna can be heard on the recording, contradicting an earlier reviewer [16]
- Phil and Ned are marked in Playin' In The Band, and the encore was Eyes Of The World [5]
- An unusual show that feels almost like two first sets [8]
- The show has no space and no long jams; the band seems focused on the songs [10]
- Reviewer hears the band content without Donna, a refreshing change for the era, in a tight, unusual show [11]
- Reviewer is glad to hear no Donna wailing here, unlike other shows of the period [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-07-27.132188.southern.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Unknown; source: unknow gen audience recording > ? > FLAC [1]
- **gd1974-07-27.akgd200e.unk.sirmick.132282.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: Audience Recording > AKG D200e's > Sony TCC152 SD > mac > rr > dat > cdr; [2]. Also: Remaster using RX4 to adjust azimuth and phase, with all tracks speed corrected and left channel gain raised [2]
- **gd1974-07-27.sbd.miller.107804.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN [3]. Also: Remaster of shnid 2420 with pitch corrected and levels fixed, with pitch help from Joe B. Jones [3]
- **gd74-07-27.sbd.kaplan.2420.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Soundboard transferred via MR, cassette and DAT to CDR, passed along by Seth Kaplan [5]
